description:
Surfaced 2026-05-07 by MAJOR PLINY in ariadne-core-workspace during ariadne--2tz dispatch. Real bug, recurring, small fix.

## Symptom

ariadne-core-workspace .git/config exhibited internally inconsistent state:
- extensions.worktreeconfig = true (set so per-worktree core.longpaths=true would activate on Windows NTFS worktrees)
- core.repositoryformatversion = 0

Git docs require version 1 when ANY extension is set. Modern git tolerates the mismatch silently. go-git (the library bw v0.12.3 uses) does not — every bw call in the workspace failed with:

    error: open repo: core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig

## Diagnostic path

PLINY's first attempt: bump core.repositoryformatversion to 1. INSUFFICIENT — go-git rejects worktreeconfig at any format version, not just version 0.

Fix that worked (promote-and-drop):
1. git config core.longpaths true   # promote to main .git/config; applies to all worktrees
2. git config --unset extensions.worktreeconfig
3. git config core.repositoryformatversion 0   # revert; no extensions remain
4. Verify: bw prime succeeds.

Reasoning ratification (PRINCIPAL 2026-05-07): core.longpaths has no reason to vary per-worktree on Windows. Every worktree on NTFS wants longpaths enabled. The per-worktree scope was incidental, not structural. Promoting to main config restores semantic correctness AND unblocks go-git.

## Scope

1. **Audit candidate workspaces.** Known orphan-branch workspaces with the same likely setup pattern:
   - ariadne-core-workspace: ALREADY FIXED 2026-05-07 by PLINY.
   - the-stoa: UNVERIFIED — same fix likely needed.
   - Any other orphan-branch workspaces on this machine: UNVERIFIED — enumerate via 'find ~/claude_projects -name .git -type d' or equivalent and check each.

2. **For each affected workspace:** apply promote-and-drop, verify bw prime succeeds, post one-line result on this ticket.

3. **Locate root cause.** Find the workspace-creation script/skill/doc that established the broken pattern in the first place. Likely candidates:
   - the-stoa substrate doc describing orphan-branch workspace setup
   - User-level CLAUDE.md Windows-discipline section
   - Any onboarding skill that creates workspaces (tier2-project-onboarding or similar)
   Update the source so new workspaces created by the same process don't reintroduce the mismatch.

4. **Documentation.** Add a one-line diagnostic snippet to MAJOR_PLINY.md (or substrate equivalent) so the next time bw fails with the worktreeconfig error, the fix is one substrate-lookup away rather than a fresh re-derivation. Snippet:

    'bw prime fails with go-git core.repositoryformatversion does not support extension: worktreeconfig — promote core.longpaths to main .git/config, drop extensions.worktreeconfig, revert formatversion to 0.'

## Gauntlet

SKIP DAEDALUS, ARGUS, ADA, VERA, ZENO. Each affected workspace is a 3-command fix; CATO eyeball verifies post-fix bw prime works. Documentation update is a single edit to a single file with no behavior change.

## Sequencing

Not blocking xft.7 cluster work. Substrate hygiene. Recommend running BEFORE any new workspace is created (so the broken pattern doesn't propagate to a freshly-spawned workspace and silently break bw there).

## Out of scope

- bw v0.12.3 upstream fix. The go-git strictness is what it is; we adjust workspace config to match, not the other way around.
- Migration to a different bw version. Separate question.

## Empirical anchor

PLINY surface 2026-05-07 in ariadne-core-workspace; CATO verdict + ariadne--2tz close-out (PR denson/ariadne-core#20, SHA 60d7983) captured the diagnostic chain. Workspace bw config side-quest noted in PLINY's ship-surface comment.

Audit phase 1 complete (PRINCIPAL-side, no PLINY ceremony — 3-command fix per workspace).

## Sweep results (2026-05-07)

Audited all 17 workspaces under ~/claude_projects/ for the broken pattern (extensions.worktreeconfig=true + repositoryformatversion=0).

**Affected (broken pattern):**
- ariadne-core-workspace — FIXED 2026-05-07 by PLINY during ariadne--2tz dispatch.
- agent-gauntlet — FIXED 2026-05-07 by PRINCIPAL just now.

**Already correct (longpaths=true in main config, no worktreeconfig extension):**
- the-stoa
- ariadne-core-workspace (post-fix)
- agent-gauntlet (post-fix)

**Not affected (no longpaths needed, no worktreeconfig set):** OB1, agent-character-builder, agent-sheet, agent-substrate, agent-team-team, knowledgecrystal-zeotek, knowledgecrystal_site, marker, markitdown, nate_skills, remotion, test-substrate-001, unstructured, user-beadwork.

Both fixes verified: 'bw prime' succeeds in both repaired workspaces.

## Phase 2 still open

Per ticket scope, remaining work:

3. **Locate root-cause source.** Find the workspace-creation script/skill/doc that produced extensions.worktreeconfig=true. Candidates: tier2-project-onboarding skill, the-stoa substrate workspace-setup doc, any README under .claude-plugin/ that scaffolds worktrees. Update so future workspace creations use the correct pattern (longpaths in main config, no extension).

4. **Substrate documentation snippet.** Add to MAJOR_PLINY.md (or substrate equivalent) the diagnostic-fix one-liner so the next bw worktreeconfig failure is one substrate-lookup away rather than re-derivation.

These two items want a real PLINY dispatch (script-hunting + doc-editing across substrate). Not a PRINCIPAL-side 3-command fix. Keeping ticket open until phase 2 ships.

Phase 2 shipped.

## Root-cause hunt (item 1)

BARTLEBY recon (this session) covered:
- `the-stoa` repo (substrate/, app/, scripts/, docs/, .claude/, .claude-plugin/)
- `~/.claude/` user-tier (skills/, agents/, settings.json, hooks — none exists)
- Sibling repos under `~/claude_projects/` (agent-gauntlet, ariadne-core-workspace, etc.)

Search patterns: `extensions.worktreeconfig`, `git config --worktree`, `core.longpaths`, `repositoryformatversion`, `git worktree add`, `EnterWorktree`.

**Zero substrate hits.** No script, skill, hook, or doc in our control writes the broken pattern. The only worktree-creating script (`agent-gauntlet/skills/arc-management/gauntlet-arc-start.sh:143`) uses vanilla `git worktree add` to a different path shape (`~/worktrees/agent-gauntlet/<id>`) and does NOT call `git config --worktree`.

The actual cause is the Claude Code harness's built-in worktree mechanism (path shape `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<slug>` matches; documented at `~/.claude/cache/changelog.md:44, 510, 529, 1304`). Upstream issue [anthropics/claude-code#45645](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/45645) confirms: when the harness creates a worktree, it writes `core.repositoryformatversion = 1` AND `extensions.worktreeConfig = true` (a self-consistent v1 state that go-git, being v0-only, refuses to read).

**Item 1 collapsed to "no fix possible in substrate; documentation-only."** The harness behavior is upstream of our code; we can't fix it here.

Side note: `the-stoa` main `.git/config` also exhibited the broken pattern at this session's start (the phase-1 audit comment listed `the-stoa` as already-correct, but creating the `agitated-chaum-85a85e` worktree re-introduced the v1 state). I repaired it in-session before any dispatch.

## Documentation snippet (item 2)

PR: https://github.com/denson/the-stoa/pull/1
Commits:
- `a3a0b71` — initial doc landing (CATO surfaced two blocking accuracy issues)
- `1cc2e61` — corrections per CATO review (causal narrative was inverted in `a3a0b71` — fixed; cited upstream issue + git docs)

Two files touched:
- `substrate/operating-disciplines.md` §9 — full diagnostic paragraph (failure mode, three-command fix in fenced bash, teardown-cleanup pointer to upstream issue, empirical anchor)
- `substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md` §6.1 — one-line cross-ref to operating-disciplines.md §9

CATO final verdict: PASS. Recommended ship.

- BARTLEBY recon (file-clerk, citations only)
- ADA initial doc edit (commit a3a0b71)
- CATO eyeball review #1 → request_changes
- PLINY in-session corrections per `MAJOR_PLINY.md` §5 build-directly authority (small surgical edits)
- CATO eyeball review #2 → PASS
- Autonomous ship per `u--7yg.11`

DAEDALUS skipped (the snippet was pre-drafted in the ticket; design was implicit in the brief). ARGUS / VERA / ZENO skipped per ticket's own gauntlet directive.
